title: Java News Roundup: JDK 27, Open J Proxy, A2A Jakarta, Azul Payara, BoxLang, Netflix ja
gist: InfoQ's weekly Java roundup covers JDK 27's GA release and JDK 28 early access, Jakarta EE 12's staggered 2026-2027 rollout, GA releases of Open J Proxy 1.0 and A2A Jakarta 1.0, an Azul Payara 7.4.0 patch for a low-cost Jackson Databind denial-of-service flaw, and Netflix's new 'ja' CLI for incrementally adopting the Java Module System -- together showing agentic-AI support and Kubernetes-native scalability concerns increasingly built into core Java enterprise infrastructure.

insights.claim: Oracle released Java 27 as a GA version shipping a final feature set of nine JEPs, setting the newest production JDK baseline for enterprises to plan upgrades around.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprise Java teams now have a stable JDK 27 target for planning production upgrades and toolchain compatibility testing.

insights.claim: JDK 28 early-access Build 16 was released with fixes carried over from Build 15, giving developers advance visibility into the next Java release roughly six months ahead of JDK 27.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Teams tracking the Java release train can begin compatibility testing against JDK 28 features before its GA.

insights.claim: BellSoft's LibericaJDK 27 downstream distribution shipped 2,542 total fixes (2,387 from upstream OpenJDK plus 155 in JavaFX), of which BellSoft itself contributed only three, illustrating that downstream JDK distributors mostly repackage upstream OpenJDK work rather than diverge from it.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Confirms that choosing a downstream JDK distribution like Liberica is primarily a support/packaging decision, not a meaningfully different code base from upstream OpenJDK.
insights.quote: Of the overall 2,542 fixes (2,387 in OpenJDK and 155 in JavaFX), BellSoft had contributed three fixes to this release.

insights.claim: Jakarta EE 12's Core Profile is planned for release in December 2026, with the Web Profile and Platform specifications following in Q1 and Q2 2027 respectively, per Jakarta EE Developer Advocate Ivar Grimstad.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprises planning Jakarta EE 12 adoption should expect a staggered rollout across roughly two quarters rather than one simultaneous release.
insights.quote: Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile will be released in December this year. The Web Profile and Platform specifications are planned to be released in Q1 and Q2 next year
insights.locator: In his weekly Hashtag Jakarta EE blog

insights.claim: The Jakarta EE Platform project is expected to hold a vote on including Jakarta NoSQL 1.1 in Jakarta EE 12, and while the broader community is encouraged to participate, only committer votes will be binding.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Shows Jakarta EE's governance formally gates final specification decisions to a committer body even as it solicits open community feedback.
insights.locator: It is also expected that the team will run a vote

insights.claim: Open J Proxy reached GA at version 1.0.0, adding a local metadata cache for DatabaseMetaData and ResultSetMetaData, a configurable HikariCP leak-detection threshold, and an implementation of the Core JDBC Type 3 driver.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Gives teams running elastic, connection-heavy Java deployments a maturing option for JDBC connection proxying with better leak visibility.

insights.claim: Open J Proxy partnered with OmniFish in January 2026 specifically to help Java teams address database scalability challenges that arise in elastic architectures such as Kubernetes, microservices, and cloud-native deployments.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Signals JDBC connection proxying as an emerging niche as more Java workloads move to Kubernetes-native elastic scaling patterns.
insights.quote: help Java teams address database scalability challenges that arise in elastic architectures such as Kubernetes, microservices, and cloud-native deployments.
insights.locator: In January 2026, Open J Proxy partnered with OmniFish

insights.claim: WildFly shipped A2A Java SDK for Jakarta Servers 1.0.0.Final, integrating the Agent2Agent protocol into Jakarta infrastructure via CDI-discovered, @PreMatching-annotated version routing that replaced duplicated multiversion routing code.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Shows the Agent2Agent interoperability protocol reaching GA support in mainstream enterprise Java application-server infrastructure, a leading indicator of enterprise agentic-AI adoption.

insights.claim: Azul Payara 7.4.0 (Community, Enterprise 6.42.0 and Enterprise 5.91.0 editions) adds support for the Jakarta Agentic AI specification in both Payara Micro and Payara Embedded.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Another concrete sign that agentic-AI support is being built directly into core Jakarta EE application servers rather than bolted on separately.

insights.claim: Azul Payara 7.4.0 patches CVE-2026-68497, a Jackson Databind vulnerability that lets an unauthenticated attacker submit a single request of just a few megabytes and force up to several minutes of single-threaded CPU work, potentially saturating a server's worker threads.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprises running Payara with Jackson Databind should prioritize patching, since the exploit is a cheap, low-effort denial-of-service vector requiring no authentication.
insights.quote: a vulnerability in Jackson Databind that allows an unauthenticated attacker to submit a single large request, say, a few megabytes, that will force up to to several minutes of single-threaded CPU work, potentially saturating a server's worker threads

insights.claim: Payara 7.4.0 removes support for the deprecated MicroProfile OpenTracing specification, forcing teams still using the @Traced annotation to migrate to OpenTelemetry's @WithSpan annotation since there is no direct equivalent in MicroProfile Telemetry.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Teams on older Payara tracing instrumentation face a concrete forced-migration cost when upgrading to 7.4.0.

insights.claim: JHipster 9.4.0 adds Playwright as an alternative to Cypress and migrates Angular microfrontend builds away from webpack Module Federation to esbuild and Native Federation, alongside reimplementing R2DBC repositories on Spring Data R2DBC.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Reflects the broader JavaScript tooling shift toward faster, more modern build systems reaching into Java-ecosystem scaffolding tools.

insights.claim: JetBrains Ktor 3.6.0 adds automatic configuration of OpenID Connect OAuth2 flows via auto-discovery and a new dedicated OpenID Connect plugin to reduce complexity when securing services through OIDC providers.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Lowers the integration effort for Kotlin service teams adopting external identity providers.

insights.claim: Netflix introduced a new CLI called 'ja,' built on the Java Module System, giving developers a modern command-line workflow for module resolution, code conventions, source-aware symbol search, and browsable API documentation so traditional applications can grow into modular JMS applications without adopting a complex build system.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: An internal Netflix tool signaling renewed practitioner interest in incrementally adopting the Java Platform Module System years after its rocky Java 9 debut, worth watching for wider open-source uptake.
insights.quote: This will allow traditional applications to naturally grow into a JMS application without the need for a complex build system.
